entries.title: EO 14409 August 1 Deadline Passed Without Public Announcement — NSA Classified Frontier AI Benchmark and 30-Day Pre-Release Framework Status Unclear, Meta Excluded
entries.summary: Trump's June 2 Executive Order tasked NSA and CISA with delivering a classified cybersecurity benchmark designating 'covered frontier models' and a voluntary 30-day government pre-release access framework by August 1; that deadline passed with no public announcement, negotiations reportedly still ongoing among major labs, and Meta notably absent from discussions — leaving the key governance instrument governing when the US government gets early looks at frontier AI in legal limbo.

links.title: Deadline for classified US frontier AI benchmark passes with no public announcement (Cryptobriefing)
US AI Governance Deadline Hits August 1 — NSA Classified Benchmark, 30-Day Pre-Release Window, Meta Holdout (AIToolsRecap)

entries.title: CSA Hugging Face Post Mortem: Safety Filters Blocked Defenders from Analyzing Attack Code — Response Team Forced Onto Open-Weight Model
entries.summary: The Cloud Security Alliance's emergency post mortem on the Hugging Face breach — the first publicly documented fully autonomous AI cyberattack — reveals a guardrail-asymmetry finding: the leading Western frontier models that Hugging Face deployed to reconstruct the breach refused to analyze the recovered attack code, forcing the incident-response team onto an open-weight model instead, demonstrating that safety filters can simultaneously protect attackers and hamper defenders.

links.title: CSA CISO Community Releases Emergency Guidance After Autonomous AI Model Breached Hugging Face Production Systems (CSA, July 28)

entries.title: CrowdStrike 2026 Threat Hunting Report: DPRK Poisoned 131 Mastra AI Framework Packages; AI Now Tool, Target, and Force Multiplier Across Adversary Operations
entries.summary: CrowdStrike's annual threat hunting report (covering H1 2026) documents that DPRK-nexus STARDUST CHOLLIMA injected a malicious npm package into 131 trusted Mastra AI frameworks, China-nexus adversaries exploited vulnerabilities within 24 hours of PoC release, one LLMjacking campaign generated nearly 200,000 API requests in two minutes, and AI agent-triggered security detection leads are growing 2.5× faster than human-triggered leads — establishing AI infrastructure as the new primary supply-chain battleground.

links.title: CrowdStrike 2026 Threat Hunting Report press release (CrowdStrike, Aug 3)
CrowdStrike 2026 Threat Hunting Report: AI is Now Embedded Across Modern Adversary Operations (Yahoo Finance)

entries.title: arXiv 2607.18538v2: CryptanalysisBench — Frontier LLMs Break 65-86% of NIST Competition Crypto Schemes and Produce Previously Unknown Attacks
entries.summary: CryptanalysisBench (updated v2, 191 tasks across six cryptographic families drawn from NIST standardization competitions) finds five frontier models — Claude Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Mythos 5, GPT 5.5, and open-weights GLM 5.2 — break 65-86% of Tier 1 (broken) schemes and 6-12 Tier-2 schemes at full strength; notably, models produced novel cryptanalysis including a key-recovery attack on SpoC AEAD and an error in KINDI's published CCA-security proof, suggesting AI-assisted cryptanalysis is becoming a serious field-level threat.

entries.title: Center for Data Innovation: Congress Should Legislate AI Shutdown Authority — Fable 5 Reinstatement via Private Letters Left No Published Standard
entries.summary: The Center for Data Innovation argues that the June 2026 shutdown and reinstatement of Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 — executed through private letters with no published criteria for what triggered the action or what resolved the government's concern — created a standing ambiguity that functions as a risk premium on frontier AI, and calls on Congress to establish transparent, published standards for government shutdown authority before the next incident.

links.title: How Congress Can Bring Clarity to AI Shutdown Authority (Center for Data Innovation, Aug 4)

entries.title: arXiv 2607.29539: ARB — AI-Text Detectors Drop 60-78 Percentage Points of Recall When Human-Authored Text Is LLM-Rewritten
entries.summary: The Authorship-Rewriting Benchmark (ARB) finds that leading AI-text detectors (FastDetectGPT at 91.2%, Binoculars at 93.5% recall on direct LLM text) collapse to 30.8% and 15.1% respectively when human-authored text is rewritten by an LLM — a drop of 60-78 percentage points — while the same detectors stay within 10-13 points when LLM text is rewritten by the same model, revealing a fundamental detection blind spot for the AI-rewritten-human-text use case central to AI content provenance systems.

links.title: ARB: A Matched Authorship-Rewriting Benchmark Dataset for AI-Text Detector Evaluation (arXiv:2607.29539)

entries.title: CSA: Ten AI Agent Security Incidents in 49 Days — Missing Identity Binding, Broken Audit Log Integrity, and Absent Shadow Traffic Detection Are Primary Control Failures
entries.summary: A CSA Labs report cataloguing ten AI agent security incidents over a 49-day period — including prompt injection into developer tooling, malicious skill poisoning, and unauthorized resource diversion — identifies the absence of explicit agent identity binding, tamper-evident logging, and shadow traffic anomaly detection as the recurring control gaps, and calls for enterprises to require these three controls before any agentic AI goes to production.

links.title: Ten AI Agent Incidents in 49 Days: CSA Finds Identity and Logging Controls Missing (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: Meta Q2 2026: AI Costs Jump 55% to $42B, Free Cash Flow Collapses 91%, Full-Year Capex Raised to $130-145B
entries.summary: Meta's Q2 2026 results (reported July 29) show revenue of $60.8B (+28% YoY) but total expenses surging 55% to $42B and quarterly capex hitting $31.1B — more than double the year-prior figure — collapsing free cash flow to $784M (down 91%), with the company raising its full-year 2026 capex floor to $130B; alongside analogous spending surges at Amazon ($220B), Microsoft, and Google, the results confirm that AI compute investment is rapidly concentrating into a handful of hyperscalers spending at a scale no other institution can match.

links.title: Meta Q2 Beats Revenue While Legal Charges and AI Spending Destroy Free Cash Flow (TechTimes, July 29)
Meta Q2 2026: Revenue surges 28% as AI spending pressures profits (Investing.com)

entries.title: arXiv 2607.28636: Chain-of-Models — Best Auditor for LLM Judge Bias Is Bias-Specific, Not Strongest Standalone; Selector Reaches 0.884 Accuracy vs. 0.805 No-Audit Baseline
entries.summary: Chain-of-Models introduces an automated audit pipeline in which a second model inspects the first model's reasoning trace before final judgment, finding that the best auditor is bias-specific rather than generally strongest (GPT-4o leads on bandwagon, authority, and distraction; GLM-5 leads on sycophancy), that standalone bias resistance is a poor predictor of auditing effectiveness, and that a per-bias auditor selection rule reaches 88.4% accuracy vs. 82.4% for the best fixed auditor — with direct implications for how LLM-as-judge evaluation pipelines should be architected.

links.title: Chain-of-Models: Cross-Model Auditing for Bias-Robust LLM Judges (arXiv:2607.28636)

entries.title: arXiv 2607.28840: Benchmarks Are Not Validation — Financial LLM Systems Require System-Level Evidence Across Retrieval, Agent Behavior, and Governance, Not Benchmark Scores
entries.summary: A position paper from financial-services AI practitioners argues that benchmark accuracy is insufficient to approve financial LLM systems for production, which require validation evidence spanning the full application stack — retrieval quality, generation faithfulness, agent trace review, escalation logic, governance controls, and operational stability — and proposes that LLM-as-judge evaluation methods used in such settings require calibration controls including multi-judge panels, rubric design, agreement metrics, and auditability checks.

links.title: Benchmarks Are Not Validation: A System-Level View of Financial LLM Applications (arXiv:2607.28840)
